section.heading: Constitutional limitations on powers and functions

content.p: Aircraft
The powers in this Act, so far as they relate to aircraft and air navigation, can only be exercised in relation to:
air navigation conducted in the course of trade or commerce with other countries or among the States; or
air navigation:
outside Australia; or
within a Territory, or to or from a Territory; or
within a Commonwealth place, or to or from a Commonwealth place; or
on aircraft owned or operated by a constitutional corporation or Commonwealth entity; or
in respect of which a State referral of power is in operation; or
in relation to any other matter with respect to which the Parliament has power to make laws; or
giving effect to an international agreement; or
matters of international concern.
Ships
The powers in this Act, so far as they relate to ships and marine navigation, can only be exercised in relation to:
marine navigation conducted in the course of trade or commerce with other countries or among the States; or
marine navigation:
outside Australia; or
within a Territory, or to or from a Territory; or
within a Commonwealth place, or to or from a Commonwealth place; or
on ships owned or operated by a constitutional corporation or Commonwealth entity; or
in respect of which a State referral of power is in operation; or
in relation to any other matter with respect to which the Parliament has power to make laws; or
giving effect to an international agreement; or
matters of international concern.
Rail vehicles
The powers in this Act, so far as they relate to rail vehicles and rail transport, can only be exercised in relation to:
rail transport conducted in the course of trade or commerce among the States; or
rail transport:
within a Territory, or to or from a Territory; or
within a Commonwealth place, or to or from a Commonwealth place; or
on rail vehicles owned or operated by a constitutional corporation or Commonwealth entity; or
on railway tracks owned or operated by a constitutional corporation or Commonwealth entity; or
in respect of which a State referral of power is in operation; or
in relation to any other matter with respect to which the Parliament has power to make laws.
Section does not limit OBR information powers
This section does not affect any powers in this Act that are expressly conferred in relation to an OBR or OBR information.
Note: The definition of OBR in section 48 applies constitutional limitations to the provisions of this Act that apply expressly to OBRs and OBR information.
Definition
In this section:

Note: A reference to Australia in any other provision of this Act includes a reference to the coastal sea of Australia: see section 15B of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.

division.heading: Establishment, functions and powers of Bureau

section.heading: Establishment of the Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB)

content.p: (1) The Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) is established by this section.
(2) For the purposes of the finance law (within the meaning of the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013):
the ATSB is a listed entity; and
the Chief Executive Officer is the accountable authority of the ATSB; and
the following persons are officials of the ATSB:
the Chief Executive Officer;
the other Commissioners;
the staff of the ATSB referred to in section 16;
persons whose services are made available to the ATSB under section 16A;
consultants engaged under section 16B;
special investigators; and
the purposes of the ATSB include:
the functions of the ATSB referred to in section 12AA; and
the functions of the Chief Executive Officer referred to in section 15A.
The ATSB consists of:
a Chief Commissioner; and
2 or more Commissioners.
The performance of a function or the exercise of a power of the ATSB is not affected by a vacancy in the membership of the ATSB.
The ATSB’s function is to improve transport safety by means that include the following:
receiving and assessing reports of transport safety matters, reportable matters, and other safety information that is prescribed by the regulations;
independently investigating transport safety matters;
identifying factors that:
contribute, or have contributed, to transport safety matters; or
affect, or might affect, transport safety;
communicating those factors to relevant sectors of the transport industry and the public in any way, including in any one or more of the following ways:
by making safety action statements;
by making safety recommendations;
by issuing safety advisory notices;
reporting publicly on those investigations;
conducting public educational programs about matters relating to transport safety;
any other means prescribed by the regulations.
The ATSB also has the following functions:
cooperating with:
an agency of the Commonwealth, a State or Territory that has functions or powers relating to transport safety or functions affected by the ATSB’s function of improving transport safety; and

a person who has, under a law of the Commonwealth, a State or Territory, functions or powers relating to transport safety or functions affected by the ATSB’s function of improving transport safety; and
a national authority or other body of another country that has functions or powers relating to transport safety or functions affected by the ATSB’s function of improving transport safety;
doing anything incidental to its function of improving transport safety.
The following are not functions of the ATSB:
to apportion blame for transport safety matters;
to provide the means to determine the liability of any person in respect of a transport safety matter;
to assist in court proceedings between parties (except as provided by this Act, whether expressly or impliedly);
to allow any adverse inference to be drawn from the fact that a person was involved in a transport safety matter.
However, even though blame or liability may be inferred, or an adverse inference may be made, by a person other than the ATSB, this does not prevent the ATSB from carrying out its functions.
To avoid doubt, subsection (3) does not prevent the prosecution of any offence under this Act.

section.heading: Independence of the ATSB and Chief Commissioner

content.p: Subject to section 21, the ATSB is not subject to direction from anyone in relation to the performance of its functions or the exercise of its powers.

The Chief Commissioner is not subject to direction from anyone in relation to the exercise of his or her powers. However, when exercising his or her powers, the Chief Commissioner must act consistently with the ATSB in the performance of its functions or the exercise of its powers.
Note: This means that the ATSB and the Chief Commissioner would not, for example, be subject to direction from anyone in relation to:
how a particular investigation will be carried out; or
the content of a public report on a particular investigation.
In exercising powers under this Act, the ATSB and the Chief Commissioner must have regard to the desirability of minimising any resulting disruption to transport by means of transport vehicles.

The ATSB must ensure that the ATSB’s powers under this Act are exercised in a manner that is consistent with Australia’s obligations under international agreements (as in force from time to time) that are identified by the regulations for the purpose of this section.

The Chief Commissioner must ensure that the Chief Commissioner’s powers under this Act are exercised in a manner that is consistent with Australia’s obligations under international agreements (as in force from time to time) that are identified by the regulations for the purpose of this section.

In exercising powers under this Act, the ATSB and the Chief Commissioner must also have regard to any rules, recommendations, guidelines, codes or other instruments (as in force from time to time) that are promulgated by an international organisation and that are identified by the regulations for the purposes of this section.

section.heading: Minister may give the ATSB notices about its strategic direction

content.p: The Minister may, by written instrument, notify the ATSB of the Minister’s views on the appropriate strategic direction for the ATSB.
Subject to section 12AB, the ATSB must have regard to a notification given under subsection (1).
A notification given under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.
The Chief Commissioner is to be appointed by the Minister by written instrument, on a full-time basis.
Note: The Chief Commissioner is also the Chief Executive Officer: see section 15.
Other Commissioners are to be appointed by the Minister by written instrument, on a part-time basis.
A person is eligible to be appointed as a Commissioner only if the person has a high level of expertise in one or more areas relevant to the ATSB’s functions.
A person’s appointment as a Commissioner is not invalid because of a defect or irregularity in connection with the person’s appointment.
The Chief Commissioner holds office for the period specified in the instrument of appointment. The period must not exceed 5 years.
A part-time Commissioner holds office for the period specified in the instrument of appointment. The period must not exceed 3 years.
Note: A Commissioner is eligible for reappointment: see section 33AA of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.

A Commissioner is to be paid such remuneration as is determined by the Remuneration Tribunal. If no determination of that remuneration is in operation, the Commissioner is to be paid such remuneration as is prescribed.
A Commissioner is to be paid the allowances that are prescribed.

The Chief Commissioner has the recreation leave entitlements that are determined by the Remuneration Tribunal.
The Minister may grant to the Chief Commissioner leave of absence, other than recreation leave, on the terms and conditions as to remuneration that the Minister determines.
The Chief Commissioner may grant leave of absence to a part-time Commissioner on the terms and conditions that the Chief Commissioner determines.
The Chief Commissioner must not engage in paid employment outside the duties of the Chief Commissioner’s office without the Minister’s written consent.
A part-time Commissioner must not engage in any paid employment that conflicts or may conflict with the proper performance of his or her duties without the Minister’s written consent.
A Commissioner may resign by giving to the Minister a signed notice of resignation.
If the Chief Commissioner resigns, he or she also resigns his or her position as the Chief Executive Officer.
Note: Subsection (2) does not prevent a person who is both the Chief Commissioner and the Chief Executive Officer from being re-appointed only as a part-time Commissioner.
The resignation takes effect on the day on which it is received by the Minister or, if a later day is specified in the resignation, on that later day.
